classification.reason: The callback is not drawn from a finite source-identifiable set in this crate: it is the `cb` parameter of the exported OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities, declared as OSSL_CALLBACK * in the public header, and the crate forwards that exact value through the provider dispatch. The target set is unbounded by the C ABI, so CLOSED SET is false; the forwarding chain is documented and checkable, so UNPROVED is too weak.
classification.not_closed_set: The public API admits any application callback, and the exported symbol is in .dynsym; the in-image callers (ssl/t1_lib.c, apps/list.c) contribute a finite subset, not the whole set.
classification.b46_b47_distinction: This is not the B46/B47 shape. B46/B47 claimed a documented caller duty (cross-thread exclusivity of SSL_CONF_CTX) that the authority did not actually document; the statements were advisory and the verifier could not check the duty from the crate's code. Here the obligation is the declared C parameter type of an exported function, and the verifier checks the crate's own side: the four operands are exactly that parameter, forwarded unchanged across the dispatch, with no in-image writer substituting a target. This is the same shape as the already-admitted ABI_CONTRACT_EXPORT_CALLBACK class (47 sites), one dispatch hop further from the C ABI.

documents.text: int OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities(const OSSL_PROVIDER *prov, const char *capability, OSSL_CALLBACK *cb, void *arg);
OSSL_CORE_MAKE_FUNC(int, provider_get_capabilities, (void *provctx, const char *capability, OSSL_CALLBACK *cb, void *arg))

OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities() provides information about the capabilities supported by the provider specified in I<prov> with the capability name I<capability>. For each capability of that name supported by the provider it will call the callback I<cb> and supply a set of L<OSSL_PARAM(3)>s describing the capability. It will also pass back the argument I<arg>.

The provider_get_capabilities() function should call the callback I<cb> passing it a set of L<OSSL_PARAM(3)>s and the caller supplied argument I<arg>. ... If a provider supports multiple capabilities with the given name then it may call the callback multiple times (one for each capability). ... It should return 1 on success or 0 on error.

contract.type_obligation: The application supplies a valid OSSL_CALLBACK function pointer (int (const OSSL_PARAM params[], void *arg)).
contract.lifetime_obligation: The documents do not state a lifetime beyond the call; the C ABI requires the pointer to be valid when the provider invokes it, which happens synchronously inside OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities. The crate does not retain cb.
contract.invocation_obligation: The provider calls cb once per capability (TLS-GROUP: one row per group; TLS-SIGALG: one row per signature algorithm), passing the caller's arg unchanged and stopping at the first zero return.
contract.verifier_check: The per-call-site witness proves: (1) each of the four operands is exactly parameter 2; (2) the function is the default provider's FUNC_PROVIDER_GET_CAPABILITIES entry; (3) the exported OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities is in .dynsym with parameter 2 declared OSSL_CALLBACK; (4) src/provider/mod.rs and src/provider/activate.rs forward cb unchanged. Any missing link refuses the witness and the site stays target-bounded.
contract.null_case: The authority calls cb with no NULL guard; the crate returns 0 on NULL. This is a recorded compatibility divergence (a C-invalid input in the authority), not a target bound.

rule.scope: Per call site: the function must be exactly ossl_prov_get_capabilities and the site operand must be exactly parameter 2. There is no name-only or shape-only absorption.
